interactions.note: The affinity of epitope specific Fab A6.2 for binding to the MNV-1 capsid protein P domain was determined by surface plasmon resonance. Point mutations Y295K, A382G, A382K, A382R and D385E abolished binding by SPR, ELISA and Western blot and mutation F297A abolished binding by SPR and Western blot.

The epitope-specific Nano-25 bound to norovirus GII.10 P domain and VLPs, and did not cross-react with GII.1, GII.4 (NSW-2012) or GII.12.
The affinity of epitope-specific Nano-25 for the norovirus GII.10 P domain was determined by isothermal calorimetry.

The epitope-specific Nano-85 bound to norovirus GII.10 P domain and VLPs, and cross-reacted with GII.4 (NSW-2012) and GII.12 and weakly with GI.1. Nano-85 was also shown to recognize GII.4, GII.10 and GII.12 in a sandwich ELISA and could detect GII.4 in clinical stool specimens from patients with sporadic gastroenteritis.

The epitope-specific Nano-85 /GII.10 VLP complexes were purified on a Ni-NTA affinity chromatography column and analyzed by SDS-PAGE, ELISA and EM. The results indicated that Nano-85 binding interaction caused the VLPs in the complex to disassemble.

The epitope of 10E9 Fab on the Norovirus Hu/GII.4 NSW-2012 P domain was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. The asymmetric unit contained two P dimers and four Fab molecules.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 2.78 angstroms

The epitope footprint of A20 Fab' on AAV-2 was determined from the previously determined crystal structure of AAV-2 by fitting a homology model of A20 Fab’ into the experimental cryo-electron microscopy density of the complex, reconstructed to a resolution of 8.5 angstroms. The asymmetric unit contains only one subunit of the antigen that is comprised of three subunits. The epitope residues are located on all three subunits, thus the curated structure provides only a partial epitope that consists of residues on the subunit A.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 8.5

The structure of 5B18 Fab in complex with norovirus GII.10 P domain was determined by molecular replacement. There were two P domain monomers and two 5B18 Fabs in the asymmetric unit; these were related by a noncrystallographic 2-fold. The 5B18 Fab was shown to bind to the wall of the P1 subdomain and involved a monomeric interaction with the P1 subdomain.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 3.3 angstroms

Epitope-specific 5B18 IgG cross-reacted with VLPs from three GII norovirus genotypes (GII.4, GII.10 and GII.12) by ELISA and Western blotting. 5B18 IgG bound to GII.10 VLPs over a range of pHs (5.3 to 9.3) with nearly identical efficacy, indicating the mAb can detect nominally intact GII.10 VLPs as at high pH (8.3-9.3) the VLPs become partially broken.

The epitope of Fab14 on CPV capsid protein 2 was determined from cryo-EM reconstruction of the Fab 14-CPV complex refined to a 3.2-Å–resolution map, using icosahedral symmetry averaging. Two samples of Fab 14–CPV complexes were separately prepared. One of the resulting complexes, described here [PDB: 7M3L] had near saturation of the Fab binding sites, whereas the other showed only partial Fab occupancy [PDB: 7M3N].
